title: Robust Satisficing Ensemble: Scalable Model Aggregation Under Distribution Shifts
claim: Combining stable and high-peak models via fragility-aware weighting keeps accuracy high under increasing distribution shift, where standard robust weighting collapses.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared shift-severity axis, shaded gain gap in final panel
description: Three side-by-side plots with a shared x-axis of shift severity α from 0 to 1. Panel (a), 'Individual model profiles', shows accuracy curves for constituent models. A thick blue line with circles (RSE, ours) sits on top. A dashed green line with squares (f_stable) is flat at about 0.70. A dashed red line with triangles (f_peak) starts high and decays. Faded orange, pink and cyan curves show the other models, some falling steeply. Panel (b), 'Weight assignment', has two stacked bars, DRO and RSE. DRO puts most weight on cyan. RSE gives more weight to green and red, the stable and peak models. Panel (c), 'Ensemble performance under shift', compares the blue RSE curve with a dashed purple DRO curve. Light blue shading between them is marked with a double arrow labeled Δ_gain. The eye goes first to the thick blue RSE curve.
caption: RSE combines stable and high-peak models to prevent catastrophic failure. (a) Constituent models face a trade-off between high initial accuracy that decays rapidly (fpeak, dashed red triangles) and lower, stable performance (fstable, dashed green squares). The faded solid lines represent the remaining active constituent models participating in the ensemble. The resulting RSE ensemble (thick blue with circles) consistently outperforms individual models across the entire shift trajectory. (b) Colors match (a). While DRO yields a suboptimal weight allocation, RSE explicitly minimizes fragility to strategically balance highly stable and high-peak predictors. (c) This integration allows RSE to maintain superior, stable accuracy across all shift severities α, achieving a significant gain (∆gain) over DRO, which collapses alongside its fragile components. (Note: Visualizations reflect actual empirical results on the TREC dataset. See Section 4 for detailed setups and benchmarks.)
abstract: Standard ensemble methods can improve robustness by mitigating individual model stochasticity, but they frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution, leaving systems vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) data. We introduce the Robust Satisficing Ensemble (RSE), a scalable probabilistic aggregation framework designed to secure model combinations by minimizing their fragility against distributional changes. By bridging a robust satisficing objective with a quadratic risk surrogate, RSE derives an analytical inner adversary. This fundamental reformulation enables highly efficient weight updates without the computational bottleneck of standard minimax optimization, crucially decoupling optimization complexity from sample size to scale effectively to large datasets. In particular, we prove a geometrically decaying truncation error for the fragility approximation via Lagrange-Burmann expansion and establish stationarity guarantees for RSE. We evaluate RSE across a comprehensive spectrum of distribution shifts, including adversarial label shift (SST-5, TREC), natural subpopulation and temporal shifts (CivilComments, HuffPost). Our results demonstrate that RSE consistently outperforms strong robust baselines, including GroupDRO, IRM, and SRM. These findings establish RSE as a practical, theoretically grounded safeguard for reliable model aggregation in dynamic environments.
